correctness.rationale: González–Hernando–Mora Proposition 1 forces every equalizer set to contain an entire bipartition class A or B. B has 2q vertices and equalizes every pair in A using an arm vertex (requires q>=3 for two noncentral v_i). For S containing A, if two u_i are omitted, each corresponding w_i must be selected: for unselected u_i_prime and w_i the sole equidistant vertex is the unselected middle u_i of their length-four path, so no valid equalizer otherwise. This yields >=2q and forces either B or exactly A plus q-1 of the u_i. Directly checked sufficiency of these q extra bases; independent brute subsets q=3,4 gave precisely 4 and 5 optima of size 2q. All-q proof is the bipartite dichotomy plus unique midpoint, not finite extrapolation.

The foundational full text treats bipartite lower bounds, stars/bistars, paths and cycles but not length-three q-arm spiders; the later paper treats lexicographic products and NP-completeness, not the tree family. The smaller partite class has q+1 vertices, yet eqdim is 2q, showing unbounded gap q-1.
